newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on tough export competition.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on tough export competition.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower amid aggressive export competition by other wheat producing countries, traders said.
Algeria and Jordan bought a combined 300,000 tonnes of wheat over the last 24 hours -- none of it from the U.S.

"That business by the French, Argentinians and then the Australians plagued us all day," a trader said. "We had a short-covering rally late but then it ended and we went back down near the lows of the day."
Traders said the traded December/March spread narrowed from 22 to 20 cents per bushel.
KCBT wheat closed one to 6-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with Dec down 6-1/4 cents at $4.32-1/2.
The players' sheet showed CIS bought 1.8 million Dec bushels. FIMAT sold 1.2 million July. Term Commodities bear-spread one million March/Dec at between 20-1/2 and 22 cents.
